reason: The text describes a reversal of the pattern stated. When the Hebrew people suffer greatly (after Pharaoh increases their work quota while removing straw provision), the Hebrew supervisors blame Moses and Aaron, saying 'you have made us abhorrent in the sight of Pharaoh' (וַיֹּאמְר֣וּ אֲלֵהֶ֔ם...הִבְאַשְׁתֶּ֣ם אֶת־ רֵיחֵ֗נוּ). Moses responds by appealing to God, not by blaming the people. There is no evidence in this passage of the leaders telling the people that their suffering is their own fault; rather, the people hold the leaders accountable for worsening their condition.
